prompt:
Desktop application UI screenshot, 1536x1024 landscape, for "MLV Studio", a scientific tool for measuring line drawings. Visual world: the calibrated psychophysics display. The entire application ground is a uniform mid-grey #7F7F7F like a mean-luminance experiment screen; white stimulus windows are the only bright surfaces; chrome is grey-on-grey with light grey and near-white text in a plain workhorse sans with tabular figures; a thin red fixation cross is the cursor; colour appears ONLY inside stimulus windows and legends as data encoding (orientation coloured with a smooth cyclic map over 0–180°). Real readable English UI text, flat, crisp, production quality, no device frame, no people.
Composition: stimulus lab comparison. Two white stimulus windows side by side in the grey field, labelled "HIGH CURVATURE" and "LOW CURVATURE", each showing a subset of contours from the same line drawing of a house, tree and fence (black lines on white). Above them a single control row: criterion "curvature", fraction slider "0.50", buttons "Split" and "Export". Below them a matching report table in grey-on-grey: rows Total length, Orientation distribution, Spatial coverage, Contour count; columns High, Low, Difference, Tolerance, and a small status mark per row (two rows pass, one marginal amber). Left: a narrow grey rail listing drawings as small white thumbnails. A footer line shows an R code snippet: split_contours(house1, property = "curvature", fraction = 0.5).
